objective: Prove a cut-vertex reduction preserving nonexistence of a matching cut, girth and the strict average-degree bound; attack unjustified stronger restrictions.

atomic_claims.text: For a connected graph split at a cut vertex, the graph has a matching cut exactly when one vertex-piece does; the cut extension is explicit.
At least one cut-vertex piece has strictly smaller average degree than the connected graph; its order decreases and its girth does not decrease.
For fixed d,g the n>=2 assertion is equivalent to its 2-connected restriction. The literal nonempty-graph assertion additionally retains the MC(K1) conjunct.
Adjacent degree-two vertices in a triangle-free simple graph give an explicit two-edge matching cut.
The K3/K5 vertex wedge invalidates arbitrary-block density inheritance; K(2,3) invalidates inferring minimum degree three from the stated girth-four residual conditions.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs, both shores nonempty, empty crossing matching allowed, forest girth +infinity.
All n>=2 and 2-connected restrictions are explicit subsidiary statements, not contract amendments.
The cut-vertex pieces are induced by one component of G-x together with x; density selection uses a minimum-average piece.
Only elementary finite-graph counting and order induction are used.
risks: Nonterminal ambiguous_problem_contract is retained from C01; no root upgrade is made.
A bound on global average degree is not automatically inherited by an arbitrary block.
K(2,3) is a girth-four attack; it does not by itself exclude separately justified girth-at-least-five reductions.
No mathematical verifier, solver or repository command was run; artifact hashing is not a correctness check.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: The proposed inference from 2-connectivity, girth four and no adjacent degree-two vertices to minimum degree at least three fails on K(2,3). This rejects only that stronger inference, not the admitted audit route.
